questions.question: What is a biome?
choices: A boundary marking one country's laws
A broad ecological region with characteristic climate and living communities
A map showing only road distances
A single species found in every habitat

questions.question: Which biome is generally warm and wet throughout the year?
choices: Tropical rainforest
Arctic tundra
Temperate desert
Boreal forest

questions.question: Which term is another name for boreal forest?
choices: Savanna
Chaparral
Steppe
Taiga

questions.question: Which biome is defined primarily by very low precipitation rather than by heat alone?
choices: Temperate forest
Tropical rainforest
Desert
Freshwater wetland

questions.question: Which biome commonly contains grasses with scattered trees and distinct wet and dry seasons?
choices: Tropical savanna
Arctic tundra
Boreal forest
Temperate rainforest

questions.question: Which forest type commonly includes broadleaf trees that shed leaves seasonally?
choices: Tropical evergreen forest
Temperate deciduous forest
Mangrove forest
Boreal coniferous forest

questions.question: What is permafrost?
choices: A glacier that floats on seawater
Snow that melts every afternoon
Ground that remains frozen for at least two consecutive years
Rain that freezes only while falling

questions.question: Why do temperature and precipitation matter when identifying terrestrial biomes?
choices: They determine every political boundary
They make soils identical in every location
They eliminate the effects of elevation
They influence which plants can grow and survive

questions.question: Why are trees generally scarce in Arctic tundra?
choices: Cold conditions, a short growing season, and frozen ground limit tree growth
The region receives strong tropical sunlight year-round
Its soils are always deeper than those in forests
All plants require temperatures below freezing to grow

questions.question: Why can grasslands support grazing and some forms of farming?
choices: Grasslands have no seasonal water limits
Grasses provide forage, and some grassland soils are fertile
Every grassland has identical soil depth and rainfall
Grassland vegetation prevents all agricultural activity

questions.question: How can deep roots help plants survive in seasonal grasslands?
choices: They prevent every possible drought
They eliminate the need for soil nutrients
They make all plants immune to fire
They help plants reach water and regrow after disturbances

questions.question: Why can clearing a tropical forest affect communities beyond the cleared site?
choices: Forest change cannot influence rivers
Only the color of the landscape changes
It can alter water movement, habitats, and stored carbon
It guarantees higher rainfall in every nearby region

questions.question: How does a biome differ from a small local habitat?
choices: A biome covers a broad region containing many habitats
A biome must contain exactly one species
A habitat is always larger than a continent
A biome is defined only by its political government

questions.question: Why can mountain vegetation change with elevation?
choices: Higher slopes always receive more sunlight and heat
Temperature and growing conditions change as elevation rises
Elevation determines the legal status of every plant
Mountain soils remain identical at every height

questions.question: Why might biome boundaries appear gradual rather than sharply divided?
choices: Plants cannot grow near national borders
Every biome must be surrounded by a road
Climate and vegetation change only at ocean coastlines
Environmental conditions can shift gradually across transition zones

questions.question: A place is cold, treeless, and has a short growing season with widespread permafrost. Which biome best fits?
choices: Tropical savanna
Temperate deciduous forest
Arctic tundra
Tropical rainforest

questions.question: A student says all deserts are hot. Which example would most directly challenge the claim?
choices: A cold region receiving very little precipitation
A warm forest receiving daily heavy rain
A tropical wetland with permanent standing water
A humid coastal forest with mild temperatures

questions.question: Two nearby slopes receive different amounts of rain because a mountain blocks moist air. What result is plausible?
choices: Both must have identical vegetation
Different vegetation communities can develop on the two slopes
The mountain removes every local climate difference
Both slopes must belong to different countries

questions.question: A community wants to compare land uses in a dry grassland. Which evidence is most relevant?
choices: Average household income without environmental data
Population totals without information on proposed land uses
Rainfall, soils, vegetation, and the demands of proposed activities
Road distances without information on water or soils

questions.question: Which conclusion best connects biome study with human geography?
choices: Biomes determine one inevitable culture in each region
Technology makes every environmental condition irrelevant
Political borders always follow biome boundaries exactly
Environmental conditions shape opportunities and limits without fully determining human choices
